..
Issued at 1216 PM CDT Wed Jul 29 2026

We have mainly quiet weather out there early this afternoon with
some patchy diurnal cumulus clouds (notably some cloud streets
up in the Arrowhead) as well as a single storm that has popped
up around Lake of the Woods. In addition to that, there is a
general haze in the sky from wildfire smoke, especially in
north-central Minnesota. This is expected to spread east, giving
the sky a hazy appearance likely into tonight. 

For this afternoon, expect mainly quiet and hot weather. A heat
advisory remains in effect through the afternoon with highs in
the upper 80s to low 90s expected. The main trick for this
afternoon will be monitoring for isolated pop-up showers and
storms. The environment out there is already and will continue
to be quite unstable with SBCAPE in the 1-2+ kJ/kg range. Bulk
shear isn't very strong, but there is up to ~30 kt and most of
that in the lower atmosphere with southeast winds at the surface
and northwest winds aloft. DCAPE is also quite high with just
over 1 kJ/kg in north-central Minnesota. But, synoptic lift is
going to be pretty weak with just a few ripples within the
broader ridging aloft. The entire model sounding profiles for
this afternoon generally look too dry for much thunderstorm
development, but if we could get any to pop, then there is a
small chance we could see some strong winds or maybe a little
hail. That risk will persist into this evening along the
Canadian Border, where eventually warm air advection and some
more pronounced cyclonic vorticity advection aloft should
promote more synoptic development of showers/storms in general.
We'll likely go from this small/isolated severe chance through
early evening into a more widespread chance of rain up that way
but with decreasing severe chances gradually into tonight as we
lose both instability and shear.

Thursday morning, a little more of the same for a while with
some showers/storms roughly along the Canadian Border while most
other places may be dry. Exact placement could vary though, so
even as far south as the Iron Range has at least a chance of
morning rain. Everywhere else, clouds will be on the increase.
Ahead of the clouds, we'll have plenty of warm air advection and
partial sunshine for a while, so another hot and muggy summer
day is expected. Widespread highs in the 80s are expected. The
current forecast is close to criteria that would justify another
heat advisory, but we will hold off for now since it should be a
touch cooler tomorrow compared to today and the increasing
clouds and rain chances support that we may not need one. 

Thursday afternoon and evening, we will have more robust
synoptic forcing aloft with a broad trough passing through.
Surface low pressure will pass by to our south and a cold front
will swing through on the backside Thursday night. As a result,
expect some widespread rain and embedded thunderstorms. We
should have plenty of instability in place in the afternoon and
evening, but almost nothing for shear. One concern is that we
could end up with a line of storms out ahead of the cold front,
which would introduce a marginal damaging wind threat. Some
large hail can't be ruled out as well. 

We've been watching for a low-end potential for flooding as well
with widespread synoptic rain and embedded storms close to the
low pressure center. Models continue to favor southern Minnesota
into Wisconsin for the heaviest rain overall, where some
widespread 1"+ amounts may fall. Up here, we will be dealing
with more of the scattered thunderstorm variety. Some places
could definitely see an inch or two of rain from thunderstorms,
but widespread amounts will likely be less than an inch and many
places may only see ~0.1-0.3". 

Lingering rain should see its way out on Friday with some non-
severe storms lingering in Wisconsin Friday afternoon and early
evening. Temperatures will fall closer to normal Friday and into
the weekend. We'll find ourselves on the far eastern side of a
broad ridge to the west, so quiet weather is looking likely
through the weekend. We'll have some onshore flow Saturday, then
a return to more southerly flow Sunday.

Next week, more southerly flow and warm air advection, so
temperatures will trend a bit upwards again. It's looking like
we may have another cold front swinging through going into
Tuesday, so perhaps some more shower/storm chances followed by a
brief cool down. Then rinse and repeat with more warmer air to
end the week and then perhaps another low pressure system
sometime late-week into the weekend to bring some more rain
chances.
